searchText: Tbh those comments were made even before TStore went live on mainnet, so we didn't have any data on the usage of tstore at all, still don't have much. I assume that you'd only protect methods that do either an sstore or an mstore or a call? I would like to know if the gas costs are that prohibitively expensive then. A good way of showing this imo would be to show the total gas cost of some popular example transactions (interact with a dex, get sandwiched, wrap and unwrap eth, send a token, use a proxy, etc) Also this was said before the idea of a small fork for pectra went out of the window safest is to protect everything 🙂 there is "view-only" reentrancy, so you would at least want to provide view reentrancy protection on all methods Too cheap. But waiting for someone else to note the problem too. why do you think it is too cheap? based on benchmarking? Based on the gas cost incevtives i don't follow
